selected_source_artifact.selection_reason: The artifact has an unusually clean reversible semantic architecture: source image -> grayscale/circular mask -> counted perimeter pins -> thread/chord network -> reconstructed likeness. This makes it suitable for a strict JANUS forward/reverse audit rather than a purely symbolic comparison.

reverse_pass.reason: Forward conversion discards color and off-circle information and uses greedy/randomized finite sampling, so exact inversion is impossible from the stored polyline/sequence alone.

janus_tranception.janus_core_result: IMAGE -> NETWORKED_LIKENESS -> INFERRED_IMAGE closes at the semantic class of likeness/image, but not at exact identity. This is a genuine asymmetric Janus loop rather than a perfect reversible transform.

egyptian_hieroglyphic_projection.method: Map only operational semantic nodes to attested Ancient Egyptian lexemes. This is a lexical/process analogy, not a claim that Egyptians used this string-art algorithm.

nodes.note: TLA also links this lexical family to the semantic root 'to match, agree', which is especially relevant to reconstruction of a likeness.

nodes.meaning: to be round; to surround; to encircle
to count; to reckon; to distribute

egyptian_hieroglyphic_projection.composite_projection_forward: twt (IMAGE) -> km/ḥḏ (DARK/LIGHT CONTRAST) -> šni̯ (ENCIRCLE) -> ḥsb (COUNT) -> mn.w/ḥtr (THREAD/CORD CONNECTIONS) -> ḥḏ (BRIGHTEN USED PATHS) -> twt (LIKENESS)
egyptian_hieroglyphic_projection.composite_projection_reverse: twt (LIKENESS) -> mn.w/ḥtr (NETWORK OF THREAD CONNECTIONS) -> ḥsb (ORDERED/COUNTED POINTS) -> šni̯ (CIRCULAR BOUNDARY) -> km/ḥḏ (INFER CONTRAST) -> twt (INFERRED IMAGE)

known_cross_project_overlap.relation: The same Ancient Egyptian color node was already used in the SCOBY-D0 GREEN-vs-BLACK hieroglyphic gate; here it acquires a different operational role as the dark-error field selected by the string-art optimizer.
Matches the recently frozen meta-registry rule that a reverse pass may expose a missing edge and may not manufacture evidence. Angel passes semantic closure but fails exact information closure.

similarity_to_existing_janus_records.most_interesting_new_relation: The same twt node can legitimately occupy both ends of the semantic loop: a source image is transformed into a likeness, and the likeness can be used to infer an image. The Egyptian lexical family itself is associated with likeness/image and matching/agreement, producing a notably tight semantic mirror without implying historical technological identity.

supported: Angel.json implements a lossy image-to-string-art transform.
The reverse semantic walk can infer an image-like field from the network but cannot recover the original image exactly.
The listed Egyptian lexemes independently attest image/likeness, encircling, thread/cord, counting, black, and bright/white concepts.
not_supported: Ancient Egyptians used this Rhino/Python algorithm.
Ancient Egyptian string art encoded photographs.
Lexical overlap proves historical transmission or technological continuity.

promotion_gate: Search primary Egyptian texts and material evidence for a single local procedure combining an image/likeness with a circular boundary, counted perimeter elements, thread/cord connections, and deliberate dark/light pattern construction. Until such co-occurrence is found, keep historical-technology status UNCONFIRMED.
